Given that $∑_(n = 1)^(∞)a_{n}$ is convergent and $∑_(n = 1)^(∞)b_{n}$ is divergent, which of the following statements are true? Assume that $b_{n}$ is well-defined for $n⩾1$.

1. $∑_(n = 12)^(∞)b_{n}$ is convergent
2. $∑_(n = 1)^(∞)a_{n} + ∑_(n = 1)^(∞)b_{n}$ is convergent
3. $∑_(n = 1)^(∞)a_{n} + ∑_(n = 1)^(12)b_{n}$ is convergent

Given that $∑_(n = 1)^(∞)a_{n}$ is divergent and $∑_(n = 1)^(∞)b_{n}$ is convergent, which of the following statements are true? Assume that $a_{n}$ is well-defined for $n⩾1$.

1. $∑_(n = 10)^(∞)a_{n}$ is convergent
2. $∑_(n = 20)^(∞)b_{n}$ is convergent
3. $∑_(n = 10)^(∞)a_{n} - ∑_(n = 20)^(∞)b_{n}$ is divergent

Given that ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ is convergent and ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}$ is divergent, which of the following statements are true? Assume that ${b}_{n}$ is well-defined for $n⩾1.$

I. - $12\cdot {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ is convergent
II. - $12\cdot {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}$ is divergent
III. - ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{50}{b}_{n}$ is convergent

Given that ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ is divergent and ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}$ is convergent, which of the following statements are true? Assume that ${a}_{n}$ is well-defined for $n⩾1.$

I. - $\frac{1}{10\,000}\cdot {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ is divergent
II. - ${\sum }_{n=1}^{8}{a}_{n}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}$ is divergent
III. - ${\sum }_{n=10}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ is convergent

:knowledge-point/title: Analyzing Statements Involving Sums of Convergent and Divergent Series
